gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-tifinagh: Commanding and a bit menacing, Bloody puffs its lowercase into fat round forms. Noto Sans Tifinagh follows in rounded, inviting sans-serif letters that fill the line like inflated shapes.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Bloody swells its lowercase into fat, round forms that look pressed out of something wet and heavy. Noto Sans Vithkuqi handles the quiet work, with open throats and barely any step up to capitals.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Menacing from the first letter, Bloody lays down heavy round lowercase forms. Noto Sans Wancho then reads like thick chalk pressed hard, its sans-serif e leaving a wide gap at the terminal, which keeps pages moving.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-yi: Bloody hits hard with fat, rounded lowercase forms that demand attention before anything else. And Noto Sans Yi does the steadier work, its deep midsection and unlatched curves keeping the text easy to take in.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-traditional-nu: Noto Traditional Nushu reads like a broad-nibbed pen that never curls its strokes shut, friendly and approachable. Then Bloody storms in above it with big round lowercase, and the two settle into a lively contrast.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-numans: Bloody's most striking trait is its swollen, round lowercase, heavy as a fist. Numans follows with sans letters like tightly coiled rope, s ends hanging far from the spine and spacing pushed wide, so reading feels spread out and unhurried.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-orienta: Bloody arrives loud and heavy, all inflated round lowercase. Orienta sits below with counters that breathe like a cut reed and almost no height difference between cases, so the sans-serif text feels hushed against the shouting above.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-pt-sans-caption: Bloody leads with swollen, menacing lowercase that grabs the eye at once. PT Sans Caption does the opposite job, keeping its unclosed, inviting curves and big-bodied letters easy to take in line after line.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-questrial: Stencil-flat and stark, Questrial draws every stroke at single weight, with open curves and a lofty band of lowercase beneath short stalks. Bloody's heavy heading, by contrast, varies its line, and the sans-serif text moves along smoothly.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-radio-canada: Blunt, swollen and loud, Bloody dominates with round lowercase and a line that swells and thins. Radio Canada holds a steady stroke with no pressure variation, and every curve ends in a clear opening for easy reading.
